quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

18 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: Hydroplaning is usually caused by:

options.text: Braking too hard.
Stopping suddenly.
Turning suddenly.
Driving too fast.

questions.explanation: When you drive too fast, your tires cannot push water off the road. Your tires lose grip, and your vehicle slides on water. This is hydroplaning.

questions.question: If you see an animal on the road, what should you do?

options.text: Do nothing special.
Honk your horn.
Pass the animal as close as possible.
Drive very carefully.

questions.explanation: Drive very carefully when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly so you don't scare it.

questions.question: What should you do at a broken traffic light?

options.text: Stop and wait for it to be fixed.
Stop and wait for a police officer.
Treat it like a four-way stop.
Drive through normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is broken, treat the intersection like a four-way stop.

questions.question: How do you enter a freeway?

options.text: Signal, let freeway traffic go first, and enter at the same speed as other cars.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must let you in.
Drive slowly to watch traffic.
Always come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, let freeway traffic go first, and enter at the same speed as other cars.
questions.explanation: Signal and enter at the same speed as traffic. Always let freeway traffic go first.

questions.question: When is it illegal to drive below the speed limit?

options.text: When slow driving stops the normal flow of traffic.
When in heavy traffic in a construction zone.
Only in rural areas.
When driving in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: When slow driving stops the normal flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive so slowly that you block normal traffic flow. You can get a ticket for driving too slowly.

questions.question: When you turn right at a green light, you must:

options.text: Keep your normal speed.
Stop and look for police cars.
Let pedestrians go first.
Speed up.

questions.explanation: You can turn right or left at a green light unless a sign says no. You must let other cars and pedestrians cross first.

questions.question: If another car's high beams are pointed at you, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your high beams.
Turn off your headlights.
Honk your horn.
Flash your high beams quickly.

questions.explanation: Flash your high beams a few times. If the other driver doesn't dim their lights, look to the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: Safe speed depends on many things.
Slow driving is always safest.
The speed limit is always safe.
Speeding up is always dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safe speed depends on many things.
questions.explanation: Safe speed depends on road conditions, how far you can see, and other traffic. In bad conditions, drive slower than the speed limit.

questions.question: When you turn, you must ____ your speed.

options.text: Increase
Keep the same
Change
Slow down

questions.explanation: Slow down when turning. This lets you control your car, stay in your lane, and handle surprises.

questions.question: Teenage drivers crash more often when:

options.text: Their pet is in the car.
Adult passengers are in the car.
Other teenage passengers are in the car.
They drive alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Other teenage passengers are in the car.
questions.explanation: Teenage drivers are more likely to crash when other teenagers are in the car than when they drive alone or with adults.

questions.question: When you park on the roadway, you should:

options.text: Use your four-way flashers.
Park at an angle.
Keep your turn signal on.
Turn your lights on.

questions.explanation: If you must park on the roadway, use your four-way flashers. Leave enough space for other vehicles to pass. Make sure drivers can see your car from at least 500 feet away in both directions.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down and keep moving in your lane.
Keep driving in your lane.
Pull to the right curb and stop.
Stop exactly where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right curb and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights or hear a siren from an emergency vehicle, pull over to the right side of the road right away and stop.

questions.question: You are coming to a railroad crossing where the crossing signals are flashing. You should:

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the vehicle ahead of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing signals at a railroad crossing, you must stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail. Watch for other warning signs like crossing gates coming down or the sound of an approaching train.

questions.question: You approach an emergency vehicle that is stopped with its lights flashing. You must:

options.text: Slow down. If possible, change lanes so you will not drive next to the stopped emergency vehicle.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and continue to drive at the same speed.
Accelerate to quickly pass the stopped vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down. If possible, change lanes so you will not drive next to the stopped emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes if you safely can to give it extra space. If you cannot change lanes, slow down below the speed limit and give the vehicle as much room as possible. Always slow down and be ready to stop near an emergency scene.

questions.question: Drive below the posted speed limit when:

options.text: Anything makes conditions less than perfect.
You see a police car.
Entering a highway where there are other cars.
You are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything makes conditions less than perfect.
questions.explanation: Drive below the posted speed limit when roads are wet or slippery, when you cannot see well, or when anything else makes conditions unsafe. You can be ticketed for speeding even at the posted limit if conditions are bad.

questions.question: If an officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Follow the directions indicated by the traffic light.
Follow the directions given by the officer.
Honk at the officer.
Check to see what the cars next to them are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the officer.
questions.explanation: When an officer is directing traffic, follow the officer's directions instead of the traffic light. Officers direct traffic to keep it moving and prevent crashes.

questions.question: When you see this black and yellow sign, it means:

options.text: The road to the right is for one-way traffic only.
That due to upcoming roadwork, there is a detour to the right.
Slow down because the road ahead changes direction at an extreme angle.
There is a crossroad to your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down because the road ahead changes direction at an extreme angle.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead has a sharp curve. Slow down before the curve as much as you would at an intersection.

questions.question: The amount of space you need to cross traffic depends on the:

options.text: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
Presence of a stop sign.
Use of your turn signals.
Cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather, and how fast the oncoming traffic is moving.
